mechanism: Oral small-molecule allosteric TYK2/JH2 inhibitor intended to modulate JAK/STAT immune-inflammatory signaling, including pathways downstream of type I IFN, IL-12 and IL-23.
phase: Phase 2 in assigned ClinicalTrials.gov psoriasis study; company pipeline reports WD-890 psoriasis program in Phase 3 in China
development_status: NCT06912165 is a recruiting, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 study of once-daily WD-890 tablets in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, with estimated primary completion October 30, 2025. A related Phase 1 healthy-volunteer study (NCT06506591) is completed. Wenda's pipeline page reports WD-890 for psoriasis, lupus erythematosus and enteritis in Phase 3; no U.S. FDA approval or direct U.S. regulatory filing was identified.
expected_launch_window: China 2028 if company pipeline timing is achieved; U.S. not forecastable/2030+
clinical_summary: The assigned trial evaluates dose response at Week 16 using PASI 75 in 140 adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, with PASI >=12, sPGA >=3 and BSA >=10% eligibility thresholds. WD-890 is mechanistically aligned with the approved oral TYK2 inhibitor deucravacitinib, and preclinical literature reports activity in psoriasis, PsA, SLE and IBD models. Differentiation remains modest because no WD-890 Phase 2 efficacy results or head-to-head data versus approved TYK2 or biologic options were found.
safety_summary: No posted WD-890 clinical safety results were found for NCT06912165 or NCT06506591. The completed Phase 1 trial assessed adverse events, serious adverse events, laboratory abnormalities, vital signs, ECGs, telemetry and physical examinations after single and multiple oral doses. Preclinical publication reports tolerable toxicity, but clinical risk should be managed using TYK2 analog expectations, including infection/TB evaluation, immunization review, liver/lab monitoring, CPK/rhabdomyolysis vigilance, malignancy awareness and avoidance in severe hepatic impairment where applicable.
management_tools: Specialty pharmacy distribution with prior authorization
Coverage criteria requiring labeled moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis and systemic therapy or phototherapy candidacy
Documentation thresholds using BSA, PASI and/or sPGA aligned to label and trial populations
Step therapy or prerequisite trial of topical therapy, phototherapy, conventional systemic therapy, or preferred biologic/oral agents as allowed by policy
Quantity limit aligned to approved once-daily tablet dosing
Baseline infection/TB, immunization and hepatic/laboratory review using TYK2 analog safety controls
Continuation criteria requiring documented clinical improvement or low disease activity
evidence_gaps: No direct WD-890 price was found; annual cost uses Sotyktu/deucravacitinib oral TYK2 analog pricing.
No posted WD-890 Phase 2 efficacy or safety results were found for NCT06912165.

ClinicalTrials.gov lists the assigned study as Phase 2, while Wenda's company pipeline reports the psoriasis program in Phase 3; public source granularity is insufficient to reconcile all regional program details.
No FDA-regulated U.S. study, U.S. filing, FDA label, or U.S. launch plan was identified.
Company pipeline timing appears China-focused and may not translate to U.S. payer timing.

sources.title: A Study of WD-890 in Participants With Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis
supports: Assigned asset and sponsor Zhejiang Wenda Pharma Technology LTD.
Recruiting Phase 2 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled study in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis
Estimated enrollment 140; actual start December 31, 2024; estimated primary completion October 30, 2025; estimated study completion November 30, 2025
WD-890 tablet administered once daily in three dose groups versus placebo through Week 16
Primary endpoint is percentage of participants achieving PASI 75 at Week 16
Eligibility includes plaque psoriasis for at least 6 months, BSA >=10%, PASI >=12 and sPGA >=3
ClinicalTrials.gov oversight states the study is not FDA-regulated

sources.title: Discovery of WD-890: A novel allosteric TYK2 inhibitor for the treatment of multiple autoimmune diseases
supports: WD-890 was developed as a selective allosteric TYK2 inhibitor binding the JH2/pseudokinase domain
TYK2 mediates type I IFN, IL-12 and IL-23 signaling relevant to immune and inflammatory diseases
Preclinical studies reported therapeutic effects in SLE, psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis and IBD models
Publication reports favorable ADME properties and tolerable toxicity in preclinical work

sources.title: DailyMed - SOTYKTU (deucravacitinib) Prescribing Information
supports: Deucravacitinib is an oral allosteric TYK2 inhibitor approved for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis and active psoriatic arthritis
Recommended dosage is 6 mg orally once daily

Label warnings include hypersensitivity, infections, tuberculosis, malignancy including lymphomas, rhabdomyolysis/elevated CPK, laboratory abnormalities, immunizations and potential risks related to JAK inhibition
Most common adverse reactions in plaque psoriasis include upper respiratory infections, blood CPK increase, herpes simplex, mouth ulcers, folliculitis and acne
Pivotal plaque psoriasis trials assessed PASI 75 and sPGA 0/1 endpoints in adults with BSA >=10%, PASI >=12 and sPGA >=3

sources.title: Mass General Brigham Health Plan Sotyktu (deucravacitinib) Prior Authorization Policy
supports: Sotyktu is managed under prior authorization for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis

Coverage criteria include diagnosis, affected BSA or crucial body areas, and topical therapy trial/failure/intolerance/contraindication unless severe psoriasis warrants biologic DMARD first-line therapy
Medication is designated specialty and must be filled at a contracted specialty pharmacy
Quantity limitation is one tablet per day
Reauthorization requires documentation of improvement or low disease activity

expected_launch_window.value: China 2028 if company pipeline timing is achieved; U.S. not forecastable/2030+
expected_launch_window.method: Combined Wenda's company pipeline timing for WD-890 psoriasis with CT.gov Phase 2 status and absence of an identified FDA-regulated U.S. program.
expected_launch_window.explanation: Wenda's pipeline lists WD-890 psoriasis as Phase 3 and provides 2028 Q4 timing, supporting a China-focused 2028 launch hypothesis. The assigned CT.gov trial remains Phase 2 and non-FDA-regulated, so U.S. timing cannot be forecast beyond a conservative 2030+ monitor horizon.

annual_cost_range.method: Used Sotyktu/deucravacitinib as the closest approved oral TYK2 analog. Low equals 12 monthly fills x $6,977.91. High equals 365 days x $232.60 per tablet.
annual_cost_range.explanation: WD-890 is unpriced. Because both WD-890 and Sotyktu are oral TYK2 inhibitors for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, Sotyktu cash-price data provide the most relevant current analog before rebates, discounts, adherence effects or launch pricing differences.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted oral TYK2 mechanism, psoriasis Phase 2/3 regional progress and preclinical autoimmune activity against lack of published WD-890 clinical results and availability of an approved oral TYK2 analog.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: WD-890 could be clinically useful as an oral TYK2 option, but the mechanism is not first-in-class and no public WD-890 clinical efficacy results or comparative data were found.

budget_impact.method: Combined high chronic oral specialty analog cost with a managed moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis population and expected PA/specialty controls.
budget_impact.explanation: Per-patient annual cost could be material if priced near Sotyktu, but utilization would likely be limited by diagnosis severity, prior therapy requirements, specialty distribution and continuation criteria.

disruption_risk.method: Assessed chronic oral route, broad psoriasis population potential, current Phase 3 China signal, lack of U.S. filing, and existence of established TYK2 management analogs.
disruption_risk.explanation: An additional oral TYK2 inhibitor could affect psoriasis pathway positioning and specialty spend, but existing Sotyktu policies provide a practical analog and U.S. launch timing is unclear.

recommended_action.method: Matched action to company-reported Phase 3 China status and 2028 timing, while keeping operational work preliminary because direct clinical results, U.S. filing status and pricing are unavailable.
recommended_action.explanation: Maintain active surveillance of China Phase 3 progress, WD-890 Phase 2/3 readouts, regulatory filings and price signals; prepare analog PA and quantity-limit criteria based on Sotyktu rather than executing formulary changes now.

quality_flags: ClinicalTrials.gov condition field says 'Brief Description of Focus of Study,' but title, official title, summary and eligibility support moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.
Assigned CT.gov trial is Phase 2 and recruiting, while Wenda's company pipeline reports the psoriasis program in Phase 3; the packet preserves both source-backed statements.
No direct WD-890 clinical results or price were found; clinical differentiation and cost rely on mechanism, preclinical evidence and Sotyktu analogs.
The assigned CT.gov trial is listed as not FDA-regulated, and no U.S. launch pathway was identified.
